newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Primakov heads for Middle East.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov heads for Middle East.

text.p: Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov headed for Damascus on Monday on the first leg of a Middle East tour aimed at demonstrating Russian support for the region's shaky peace process, ITAR-Tass news agency said.
Primakov's trip, taking in Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, Israel, the autonomous Palestinian territories and Jordan, will focus on the obstacles to a comprehensive Arab-Israeli settlement, Tass said.
Foreign ministry spokesman Gennady Tarasov said Moscow considered Primakov's visit particularly important in view of Russia's role as co-sponsor in the Middle East peace process.

"We hope that contacts with the leaders of the Arab countries and Israel will help contribute to the task of bringing the peace process back on to a constructive track and to spur its participants to follow scrupulously the commitments they have undertaken," Tass quoted Tarasov as saying.

Primakov's departure coincides with fresh signs of tension between Israel and the PLO after their failure over the weekend to clinch a deal on a partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
Palestinians have said Israel is trying to renegotiate terms of the Hebron withdrawal which the Jewish state agreed to more than a year ago.
